chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has capital in a mudarabah (profit-sharing partnership) partnership, and his profit decreases, so he fears that [the capital owner] will take [his share of profit], so he increases [the profit given to] his partner beyond the condition that was between them. And he does this out of fear that [his share] will be taken from him. He said, 'There is no harm with it.'

key_terms.رِبْح: Profit: The gain generated from the partnership business.
key_terms.شَرْط: Condition: The agreed-upon terms or ratio of profit distribution.
key_terms.صَاحِب: Partner/Owner: Refers to the other party in the partnership, typically the capital provider.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm with it: A legal ruling indicating permissibility.
key_terms.مُضَارَبَة: Mudarabah: A profit-sharing partnership where one party provides capital and the other provides labor.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to increase a partner's share in a mudarabah contract out of fear of losing profit?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies a specific nuance in mudarabah jurisprudence, permitting unilateral profit enhancement by one partner to mitigate the risk of dispute or claim by the other, provided the increase is not arbitrary but driven by legitimate caution (khauf). This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on preventing unjust enrichment and maintaining harmony in commercial contracts, distinguishing between voluntary generosity and strategic concession to avoid litigation. It reflects the practical application of 'urf (customary practice) and the principle of removing hardship in financial dealings.
